name: gameplay-cinema-ai
origin: The AI running (checkpoint 4, slice c): the round of gameplay-cinema-start (seed 42, Arcade, Normal, Cinema, robot 0) with its three AI robots left alone and the player standing still. Godot's AI draws from the round's Math.random (the original's place, tests/goldens/gameplay-cinema-start/math_random.json). Every robot, bomb and frame matches through ai-30 (frame 731). The original's AI is not reproducible further: its callbacks run on the host clock (Action.setAction's TweenMax.delayedCall(0.1), AbstractState's Timer(2000), AbstractAttackState's setTimeout), so two recordings of this case already differ at round frame 10 (robot 5 turned up in one, down in the other); recorded to ai-360, Godot first differs from this recording between ai-30 and ai-60 (robot 6, Mint: another row). The goldens are this recording's first two captures.
godot_note: Godot starts on the recorded round (round cinema-start) as gameplay-cinema-start does.

wall_clock_text./@0#1/@0/time: Game.countTime counts Date seconds; the reference player's Date follows the host clock, not its stepped frames, so TIME reads 178 or 177 here depending on the machine

actions.godot_note: The app does not reproduce the menus' Math.random draws, so the round this START opens replays the original's generator from the recording (math_random.json) and rolls its board from the original's draws (Layouts.roll_set: it must equal the golden's boxes and frames); the enemy robots come from the golden of the cinema-start capture (App.round_as_recorded).

thresholds_note: No 3x frame of this recording exists (another run of the original's AI differs from frame 10), so the pixel pass line is the gameplay screen's measured 3x->1x ceiling (SSIM 0.935, as gameplay-cinema-bomb) minus 0.02, and region dE 8.
